speaker: Warren Ashford
cascadeSummary: Certified final inspection sign-offs for the Temescal Community Health Center while demanding a complete closeout audit following its public opening. Additionally, transmitted targeted municipal service requests to fortify commercial security in KONO and address sluggish street trade in Temescal through strict baseline oversight.

statements.topic: Temescal Community Health Center Opening and Final Inspection Audit
statements.decision: Formally certify final fire-rated wall and drywall inspection sign-offs while demanding full closeout audit documentation for the $45M Temescal Community Health Center.
statements.quote: The Temescal Community Health Center opened ahead of schedule not by executive magic, but because District 7 inspected every single conduit, logged every inspection, and held the budget line.
statements.fullStatement: The Mayor can cut the ribbon and hold her celebration, but the $45M Temescal Community Health Center crossed the finish line because this office refused to cut corners. District 7 verified the MEP rough-ins, cleared the certified fire-rated wall inspections, and enforced strict milestone compliance before approving drywall enclosure. Public infrastructure succeeds when oversight is rigorous, not when press releases are plentiful. As this facility opens its doors to the public, I am submitting the final certified inspection sign-offs to the clerk while demanding a comprehensive closeout audit log. We delivered a state-of-the-art facility for Temescal under strict fiscal discipline, and that standard of vigilance must govern every major capital project in Oakland.

statements.topic: District 7 Corridor Management and KONO Municipal Service Delivery
statements.decision: Advance municipal service requests for KONO commercial corridor security and demand targeted economic support to revitalize Temescal street trade.
statements.quote: KONO does not need vague mayoral promises—it requires verified municipal safety delivery and targeted corridor maintenance that protects local merchants.
statements.fullStatement: Across District 7, our neighborhood mood is clearly upbeat, but the economic realities on the ground require focused municipal delivery rather than broad executive rhetoric. While KONO maintains steady street trade and low crime, corridor confidence depends entirely on targeted municipal safety presence and property security enforcement. Meanwhile, in Temescal, where street trade has slowed despite our infrastructure wins, we need verifiable service coordination to drive foot traffic back to local storefronts. Rockridge demonstrates the resilience of our commercial core when baseline municipal services are properly maintained. I am submitting formal service requests for KONO and Temescal to ensure city departments deliver measurable baseline maintenance rather than unbudgeted executive programs.
